extra.reason: Resolved by composting rather than by choosing. A bd memory is the highest-intent record bd produces - one sentence someone decided should outlive its session, written for no other purpose - so the pile mines it from transcripts alongside commit messages and bead closes. It composts as a discovery at lower confidence than a recorded change, because a memory is an assertion with no diff behind it and may be written by an agent. bd keeps memories for priming; the pile keeps them for every other project.

The bridge reads work from bd and never writes it: bd owns beads, dependencies and the ready queue, hugel owns knowledge and accounting. Beds are located from transcript cwd rather than configuration, since a bed is already named for a working directory. Readiness comes from bd directly rather than being recomputed, so hugel's view cannot drift from the queue tenders pull from. Surfaced through hugel bed list, which now shows where each bed lives and what is ready, active and blocked there.

One screen across every bed: in flight, ready, blocked, with tab switching to the knowledge side. Built as panes on the tend model rather than a second TUI, because work and knowledge are two halves of one sitting. Read-only - bd owns starting and closing a bead. Per-bed caps keep one busy bed from burying the others, and each pane keeps its own cursor position.

A tender is an ordinary interactive agent session running detached in tmux, briefed by a file and answering with a file - not claude -p, and no send-keys. That keeps it on a subscription and leaves both the request and the outcome on disk for review. Each tender gets a worktree and branch of its own, named for the bed rather than the bead so transcript accounting stays with the project. It commits to its branch and stops: pushing, merging and closing are the gate's decisions.

A tender's brief now carries soil drawn for the bead, with the caveat that it is a survey rather than the truth. Push is right here and pull is right in interactive sessions for the same reason: where the tokens land and who is there to ask. The bead's full text scores the draw; its title labels it, because the rendered header quotes the query back into the brief.

Deleted. They describe the Postgres, DBOS and Firecracker system this rewrite exists to escape, and were never committed, so git history carries neither. What survived the plan is already in the pile as composted decisions: the ordering argument, the durable-execution reasoning, and the reason all of it was too much canopy for the roots that existed.

Work, test, review, test, then merge, push and close. The second test runs on the branch merged with the current base, which is the only test true of what gets pushed. The reviewer is a separate agent run with a different prompt and is forbidden from repairing what it finds, since doing both leaves nobody to review the repair. A review with no verdict counts as refusal - silence is not approval. Every stage refuses without cleaning up, so a failed gate leaves the work where it can be read.

Measured: bd prime --hook-json emits 6506 bytes, about 1626 tokens, injected at turn zero of every session. Carried across the 12 sessions of the last week (1461 turns) that is 2.4M context tokens, ~$1.19 of $289.29 spent, or 0.4%. Per session it ranges 0.3-0.7%. The preamble is worth it: an agent that does not know about ready work cannot pick any up, and 0.4% is not the waste worth hunting - the 86% context tax is. This also sets a yardstick for hugel's own soil budget, which at 1500 tokens is the same order of magnitude and should be held to the same test. Caveat: this prices the carrying only. Whether the preamble changes how many turns a session takes is a different and harder question, unmeasured here.

A skill that drafts beads and epics in conversation, reviews them with the user, and files only what is agreed. Filing unreviewed work fills the queue with intentions, which matters more now that tenders pull from it unattended. Most of the skill is about what makes a bead worth filing: the description carries the why rather than restating the title, because closing a bead with a reason is what the pile composts, so a bead is paid for twice.
